name: Arms Warrior

pitch.newcomer: A two-handed weapon master who lands crushing blows and knocks riders off their mounts.
pitch.veteran: Two-hander burst with Mortal Strike, Weaponmaster and Spearing Strike.

text.newcomer: Huge two-handed hits that can end a fight fast.
text.veteran: Big Mortal Strike burst; strong in world PvP.

text.newcomer: Spearing Strike knocks riders off their mounts, great against other players.
text.veteran: Spearing Strike dismounts: a Forever-only PvP tool.

text.newcomer: Victory Rush heals you after kills, so you keep moving.
text.veteran: Victory Rush (20) heals 10% on kills, which cuts downtime.

text.newcomer: Has a hard time recovering once badly hurt.
text.veteran: Poor recovery from heavy damage (Blizzard's own words).

text.newcomer: Mostly brings damage to a group.
text.veteran: Light utility beyond Battle Shout and debuffs.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Plate and Victory Rush help, but a warrior can't easily escape a fight gone wrong.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Plate + Victory Rush help, but few escapes; pull carefully.

newInForever: Bloodthrill can proc Overpower from Rend.
scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption), adjusted for Forever: Victory Rush, rage from damage no longer cut by armor, separate shorter cooldowns, Spearing Strike. Beta rage bugs make sustain and leveling less certain.

name: Fury Warrior

pitch.newcomer: A dual-wielding berserker who turns rage into a whirlwind of blades.
pitch.veteran: Dual-wield rage DPS: Bloodthirst, Raging Blows, Flurry.

text.newcomer: A classic raid damage dealer that groups love to bring.
text.veteran: Traditional top raid melee; projected high demand.

text.newcomer: Whirlwind hits with both weapons, shredding groups of enemies.
text.veteran: Raging Blows: dual-wield Whirlwind for strong AoE.

text.newcomer: Your Battle Shout now powers up your whole raid.
Death Wish makes you take more damage, so it's risky when things go wrong.
text.veteran: Death Wish raises damage taken; little self-sustain.

text.newcomer: Bloodthirst no longer heals, so you'll rest more while leveling.
text.veteran: Bloodthirst lost its heal; more downtime solo.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: High risk, high reward: you hit hard but can't take much punishment.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Glass-cannon melee; risky solo on Hardcore.

newInForever: Raging Blows (16-point): Whirlwind with both weapons.
Bloodthirst trades its heal for +10% run speed.
Death Wish now increases damage taken.
scoreBasis: Classic-era raid reputation (assumption), adjusted for Forever: Bloodthirst lost its heal, Flurry reduced, Death Wish redesigned. Raid demand is speculative until Dec 9.

name: Protection Warrior

pitch.newcomer: The classic shield-bearer: you hold the line so your friends can win.
pitch.veteran: Shield tank with Vanguard charges, Bastion and big rage tools.

text.newcomer: Tanks are always needed, so you'll find groups fast.
Shield Wall and Last Stand keep you standing through huge hits.
text.veteran: Shield Wall (15 min, own cooldown) plus Last Stand.

text.newcomer: Lots of tools to master: stances, shouts and shield skills.
text.veteran: Deep threat and rage toolkit; Charge in Defensive Stance via Vanguard.

text.newcomer: Slow when leveling alone; many level as Arms and swap later.
text.veteran: Slow solo; dual-spec Arms for questing.

text.newcomer: Not great at farming gold on your own.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Very sturdy, but slow solo leveling means more time in danger.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Durable, but slow solo; dual spec at 40 helps.

newInForever: Bastion, Master of Defense and Focused Rage talents.
Thunder Clap usable in Defensive Stance.
Shield Wall and Retaliation no longer share a cooldown.
scoreBasis: Classic-era tank baseline (assumption) plus Forever changes: Vanguard, Bastion, separate cooldowns, rage from damage taken no longer reduced by armor.

name: Holy Paladin

pitch.newcomer: A holy knight who heals with the Light while wearing heavy plate.
pitch.veteran: Single-target plate healer; Holy Shock at 21, Light's Vigil at 31.

text.newcomer: A strong single-target healer every group wants.
text.veteran: Top single-target healing; healers are always in demand.

text.newcomer: Heavy armor and healing make you very hard to kill.
text.veteran: Plate, bubble and self-heals: extremely durable.

text.newcomer: Blessings and auras make everyone around you stronger.
Leveling alone as a healer is slow; many swap specs to level.
text.veteran: Slow solo; dual-spec Ret for questing.

text.newcomer: Not built for farming gold.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: One of the safest Hardcore picks: plate, heals and a holy shield.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Divine Shield + plate + heals = top HC safety.

newInForever: Holy Shock moves to 21 points with a 10-second cooldown.
Voice of Truth makes you immune to silences and interrupts.

variants.name: Shockadin
variants.note: Blizzard positions Holy Shock as the alternative to Twist of Light for hybrid Holy damage builds.

scoreBasis: Blizzard calls Holy strongest at single-target healing, with group healing needing planning. Classic-era baseline (assumption) for leveling and farming.

name: Protection Paladin

pitch.newcomer: A holy shield-bearer who tanks with the Light and outlasts anything.
pitch.veteran: A real plate tank now: Seal of Fury, Templar's Bulwark, taunting Judgement.

text.newcomer: Templar's Bulwark can absorb your entire health bar: incredibly tough.
text.veteran: Templar's Bulwark (21): absorb equal to 100% max health.

text.newcomer: Seal of Fury shields you as you fight, so you rarely need to rest.
text.veteran: Seal of Fury absorbs plus mana returns: low downtime.

text.newcomer: Tanks are always needed, and Forever makes paladins real tanks.
text.veteran: Forever turns Prot into a real tank option.

text.newcomer: Little ranged reach, so enemies that keep their distance are a pain.
text.veteran: Limited range; no interrupts or slows.

text.newcomer: Raid tanking is unproven until raids open.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Among the toughest Hardcore picks: heavy armor, heals and an emergency bubble.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Extremely durable; strong HC pick.

newInForever: Seal of Fury (level 10): a tanking seal with absorbs and a ranged taunt.
Swift Judgement and Iron Creed talents.
Consecration's threat is capped at 4 targets.
scoreBasis: Forever deliberately turns Protection into a real tank (BLZ-PAL); scores lean on Blizzard's stated intent. Consecration's 4-target cap tempers AoE farming.

name: Retribution Paladin

pitch.newcomer: A holy crusader who mixes weapon strikes with blasts of Light.
pitch.veteran: Melee/Holy hybrid DPS: Twist of Light seal twisting, Holy Strike, Repentance.

text.newcomer: Hard to kill and steady while leveling: a safe, forgiving pick.
Brings blessings and auras that help the whole group.
Twist of Light rewards swapping seals for big empowered swings.
text.veteran: Twist of Light (31): approachable seal twisting.

text.newcomer: Raid demand is uncertain until raids open.
Little ranged reach, and no way to slow enemies down.
text.veteran: No slows, no interrupts, limited range.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Plate, heals and a holy bubble make it one of the safest ways to level.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Bubble + heals + plate: top HC leveling safety.

newInForever: Twist of Light (31-point) brings back seal twisting.
Judgement no longer consumes your seal.

variants.name: Shockadin
variants.note: Holy Shock hybrid built from Holy talents instead of Twist of Light.

scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption), adjusted for Forever's Holy Strike, seal changes and Twist of Light.

name: Beast Mastery Hunter

pitch.newcomer: Fight side by side with a loyal beast that takes the hits for you.
pitch.veteran: Pet-centric ranged DPS; the pet tanks, Summon Hawk adds burst.

text.newcomer: Your pet takes the hits while you shoot, so you stay safe.
text.veteran: The pet tanks; you shoot. Very safe solo.

text.newcomer: Levels faster and more smoothly than almost anyone.
Easy to learn and still effective.
Great at farming on your own, even tougher enemies.
Most of your power is in your pet, so you'll care for it a lot.
Brings mostly damage to groups; hunters can't stun or interrupt.
text.veteran: No stuns or interrupts; limited group utility.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: A favorite for Hardcore: the pet tanks and Feign Death gets you out.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Pet tanking + Feign Death: the classic safe HC pick.

newInForever: New Fox pet family; every family gets a unique ability.
scoreBasis: Classic-era leveling reputation (assumption) plus Blizzard's note that the pet can tank in solo and small-group content.

name: Marksmanship Hunter

pitch.newcomer: A sharpshooter who hits from extreme range, with or without a pet.
pitch.veteran: Ranged burst: Aimed and Sniper Shot, raid-wide Trueshot, petless via Lone Wolf.

text.newcomer: Lone Wolf lets you skip the pet entirely and hit harder for it.
text.veteran: Lone Wolf (11): +20% damage without a pet.

text.newcomer: Big shots from very far away.
text.veteran: Aimed Shot plus Sniper Shot burst at max range.

text.newcomer: Trueshot Aura now boosts your whole raid.
Can't shoot enemies who get right next to you.
text.veteran: 8-yard dead zone; no stuns or interrupts.

text.newcomer: Without a pet to tank, bad pulls get dangerous.
text.veteran: Petless builds lose the pet tank.

text.newcomer: Uses a pet unless you take Lone Wolf, and never centers on it like Beast Mastery does.
text.veteran: Pet by default unless Lone Wolf; never BM-level pet play.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Keep a pet while leveling for safety; go Lone Wolf when you're ready.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Pet for safety; Lone Wolf is riskier on HC.

newInForever: Lone Wolf (11-point): play without a pet.

variants.name: Lone Wolf
variants.note: Petless Marksmanship via the 11-point Lone Wolf talent.

scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption), adjusted for Lone Wolf, Sniper Shot and raid-wide Trueshot Aura.

name: Survival Hunter

pitch.newcomer: A trap-setting skirmisher who fights up close with blades and bleeds.
pitch.veteran: Melee hunter: traps in combat, Strider Kick, Lacerating Strikes, dual-wield.

text.newcomer: A real melee hunter: traps, blades and bleeding strikes.
text.veteran: Fully melee-capable hunter, new in Forever.

text.newcomer: Traps, Deterrence and Counterattack keep you alive up close.
text.veteran: Traps in combat plus Deterrence: a sturdy skirmisher.

text.newcomer: Pet plus traps make solo play smooth.
text.veteran: Strong solo with pet, traps and melee.

text.newcomer: A brand-new style, so how groups value it is still unknown.
Brings mostly damage; no stuns or interrupts.
text.veteran: Low utility; no stuns or interrupts.

text.newcomer: Fights alongside a pet by default; going without one takes the right talents.
text.veteran: Pet by default; petless needs an MM dip into Lone Wolf.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Traps and a pet give you control, but melee puts you closer to danger.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Good control, but melee exposure; play the pet.

newInForever: Survival is now a full melee spec.
scoreBasis: Low confidence: a new melee design with no Classic equivalent. Based on Blizzard's description of trap and melee builds; petless play via an MM dip into Lone Wolf is an assumption.

name: Assassination Rogue

pitch.newcomer: A poison master who strikes from stealth and lets venom do the rest.
pitch.veteran: Dagger and poison DPS: Mutilate, Venom, poison crits.

text.newcomer: Deadly ambushes on unsuspecting enemy players.
text.veteran: Strong stealth openers and poison pressure in PvP.

text.newcomer: Steady, high single-target damage for raids.
text.veteran: High single-target damage; poisons can crit.

text.newcomer: Mutilate and Cold Blood make for brutal openers.
Brings mostly damage to a group.
You'll stop to eat between fights more than most.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Stealth lets you pick your fights, and Vanish gets you out of trouble.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Stealth + Vanish: choose every engagement.

newInForever: More poison charges, and poisons stack with sharpening stones.
scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption), adjusted for Mutilate, Venom and poison crits.

name: Combat Rogue

pitch.newcomer: A straightforward duelist with a blade in each hand and endless combos.
pitch.veteran: Sword, axe or mace DPS: Hack and Slash, Blade Flurry, the simplest rogue.

text.newcomer: The easiest rogue to pick up.
Reliable damage in groups, with cleave for packs.
text.veteran: Strong sustained damage; Blade Flurry cleave.

text.newcomer: Levels steadily on its own.
Brings mostly damage to a group.
You'll stop to eat between fights more than most.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Evasion, Sprint and Vanish give you three ways out of trouble.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Evasion + Sprint + Vanish escape kit.

newInForever: Hack and Slash replaces all weapon specializations.
Puncturing Wounds can grant extra combo points.
scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption), adjusted for Hack and Slash and Expose Armor changes.

name: Subtlety Rogue

pitch.newcomer: A master of shadows and dirty tricks who controls every fight.
pitch.veteran: Control and opener rogue: Premeditation, Cutthroat, Thousand Cuts.

text.newcomer: The ultimate world PvP hunter: pick your fights and control them.
text.veteran: Top-tier stealth control and PvP burst.

text.newcomer: Devastating opening strikes from stealth.
text.veteran: Big Ambush openers; Cutthroat enables more Ambushes.

text.newcomer: Plenty of tricks to slip away when needed.
Less sought after for raids.
Hard to master: positioning and timing matter a lot.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Stealth means you choose every fight, a strong Hardcore trait.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Total control over engagements.

newInForever: Cutthroat lets Ambush work outside stealth after a Backstab.
Dirty Deeds allows Garrote from the front.
scoreBasis: Classic-era PvP reputation (assumption) plus Forever's Cutthroat and Thousand Cuts.

name: Discipline Priest

pitch.newcomer: A protective healer who shields allies before harm even lands.
pitch.veteran: Shield and absorb healer: Penance, Divine Aegis, Renewed Hope.

text.newcomer: A healer every group wants, with shields that stop damage before it hurts.
text.veteran: Healer demand plus absorbs; Penance at 21.

text.newcomer: Buffs, dispels, resurrection and Fear Ward for the tank.
text.veteran: Fortitude, Divine Spirit, dispels, Fear Ward.

text.newcomer: Shields make you tough to bring down in team PvP.
Leveling alone as a healer is slow; many swap to Shadow.
text.veteran: Slow solo; dual-spec Shadow for questing.

text.newcomer: Cloth armor and few escapes make you fragile.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Shields help, but cloth and few escapes demand care.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Shields help; still fragile on HC.

newInForever: Holy Precision removes the need for hit gear.
scoreBasis: Classic-era healer baseline (assumption) plus Forever's Penance and absorb toolkit.

name: Holy Priest

pitch.newcomer: The classic healer: pure Light, big heals and a calm presence.
pitch.veteran: Throughput healer: Binding Heal, Prayer of Mending, strong group heals.

text.newcomer: The healer every group is looking for.
Buffs, dispels and resurrection help everyone.
Big heals that rescue allies at the last second.
text.veteran: Strong direct heals; Binding Heal at 16.

text.newcomer: Slow alone; most level as Shadow and swap at 40.
Cloth armor and few escapes make you fragile.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Level as Shadow and keep Holy for groups; dual spec at 40 makes this easy.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Shadow/Holy dual spec is the HC play.

newInForever: Fear Ward and Devouring Plague for all priests.
Renew can stack from multiple priests.
scoreBasis: Classic-era healer reputation (assumption) plus Forever's Binding Heal and Prayer of Mending.

name: Shadow Priest

pitch.newcomer: A shadow caster who melts minds and drains life to keep going.
pitch.veteran: DoT and drain caster: Shadowform, Devouring Contagion, Shadow Word: Death.

text.newcomer: Drains and shields keep you fighting without rest.
Dangerous in PvP with fear, silence and pressure over time.
Wears enemies down with spreading shadow plagues.
Shadow Weaving now only helps you, not your group.
text.veteran: Self-only Shadow Weaving; less raid utility.

text.newcomer: Cloth armor and few escapes make you fragile.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Shields and Psychic Scream help, but you're still fragile in cloth.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Shield + Fear help; still cloth.

newInForever: Devouring Plague and Shadow Word: Death are baseline.
Devouring Contagion spreads to new targets.
scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption) plus Forever's Shadowform and Devouring Plague changes.

name: Elemental Shaman

pitch.newcomer: A storm-caller who hurls lightning and lava at their foes.
pitch.veteran: Spell burst caster: Lava Burst, Lightning Overload, totems.

text.newcomer: Big lightning and lava bursts that hit hard.
text.veteran: High burst: Lava Burst (31) plus Lightning Overload.

text.newcomer: Totems make your whole group or raid stronger.
A strong presence in team PvP battles.
text.veteran: Strong BG caster with Earthbound roots.

text.newcomer: Uses a lot of mana, so expect breaks between fights.
No crowd control and little armor against a determined attacker.
text.veteran: No effective CC; vulnerable when focused.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Healing spells help you recover, but you lack ways to control enemies.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Self-heals help; no real CC on HC.

newInForever: Call of the Elements drops 4 totems at once.
scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption) plus Forever's Lava Burst and totem changes. The Elemental tree was restructured again on Oct 15 (details unverified).

name: Enhancement Shaman

pitch.newcomer: A storm-charged warrior who mixes axe swings with lightning, and can even tank small groups.
pitch.veteran: Melee/spell hybrid: Maelstrom Weapon, Stormstrike, small-group off-tank.

text.newcomer: Strong, steady leveling with heals and weapon enchants.
text.veteran: Solid solo with hour-long imbues and self-heals.

text.newcomer: Instant lightning bolts after a flurry of hits.
Totems help your group, and you can even tank small groups.
Your place in raids is still a question mark.
No crowd control to fall back on.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Mail, a shield option and self-heals make for a sturdy leveler.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Mail + heals: sturdy; no CC though.

newInForever: Spirit Weapons lets you build threat with Rockbiter.

variants.name: Off-tank
variants.note: Blizzard calls Enhancement a temporary tank in small-group play (Rockbiter + Spirit Weapons).

scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption) plus Maelstrom Weapon and Blizzard's small-group tanking statement.

name: Restoration Shaman

pitch.newcomer: A healer who channels water and spirits, and buffs the group with totems.
pitch.veteran: Chain Heal and Riptide healer with the strongest totem support.

text.newcomer: Healers are always needed, and yours heal many at once.
text.veteran: Chain Heal plus Riptide group healing.

text.newcomer: Totems make everyone in your group stronger.
A powerful healer in team PvP.
Slow alone; many level as Enhancement or Elemental.
No crowd control to stop attackers.
text.veteran: No CC; weak alone in world PvP.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Mail and strong heals help, but level in a damage spec for speed.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Level Enh/Ele, heal at 40 via dual spec.

newInForever: Call of the Elements totem presets.
Several totems now buff the whole raid.
scoreBasis: Classic-era healer reputation (assumption) plus Riptide, Water Shield and raid-wide totems.

name: Arcane Mage

pitch.newcomer: A scholar of pure magic who stacks power for devastating arcane blasts.
pitch.veteran: Arcane Blast stacking burst caster with Missile Barrage procs.

text.newcomer: Builds up power for huge arcane damage.
text.veteran: Arcane Blast stacks into big burst.

text.newcomer: Brings food, water, portals and crowd control.
Strong area damage for clearing groups of enemies.
Very fragile, especially when enemies reach you.
You'll drink often between fights (but you make your own water).
text.veteran: Mana downtime, softened by conjured water.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Fragile on Hardcore; Frost is the safer mage for leveling.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Fragile; level Frost on HC.

scoreBasis: Arcane Blast was redesigned on Oct 15 (stacking spell power), so burst and complexity are uncertain. Classic-era baseline (assumption) otherwise.

name: Fire Mage

pitch.newcomer: A pyromancer who chains critical strikes into huge fireballs.
pitch.veteran: Crit-driven fire caster: Heating Up, Pyroblast, Ignite.

text.newcomer: Massive fireball hits and explosive critical strikes.
text.veteran: Crit-driven burst: Heating Up into Pyroblast.

text.newcomer: Strong, steady raid damage.
text.veteran: Strong raid DPS; Ignite is now per-mage.

text.newcomer: Brings food, water, portals and crowd control.
The most fragile mage: few ways to stop enemies reaching you.
You'll drink often between fights.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Risky on Hardcore: great damage, little defense.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Glass cannon; risky on HC.

newInForever: Heating Up: crits speed up Pyroblast.
scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption) plus Heating Up and per-mage Ignite.

name: Frost Mage

pitch.newcomer: An ice mage who freezes enemies in place and shatters them.
pitch.veteran: Control caster: Ice Lance, Fingers of Frost, Ice Block, top kiting.

text.newcomer: Freezes enemies and escapes trouble with Ice Block.
text.veteran: Frost Nova, Ice Block, Cold Snap: elite control.

text.newcomer: Pulls big groups and blasts them down: great for farming.
Slows and freezes make you a menace in team PvP.
You'll drink often between fights (but you make your own water).
text.veteran: Mana downtime, softened by conjured water.

text.newcomer: Slightly less raid damage than the other mages.
text.veteran: Projected lower raid DPS than Fire or Arcane.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: The safest mage for Hardcore: freeze, blink and Ice Block.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Best mage HC spec: control plus Ice Block.

newInForever: Ice Lance (11-point) and Fingers of Frost.
Shorter Cone of Cold to curb kite-farming.
scoreBasis: Classic-era leveling and farming reputation (assumption). Blizzard shortened Cone of Cold specifically to curb kite-farming, so farming is scored a bit lower.

name: Affliction Warlock

pitch.newcomer: A curse-weaver who drains life and lets shadows do the work.
pitch.veteran: DoT and drain caster: Wrack, Soul Siphon, DoT crits, near-zero downtime.

text.newcomer: Drains life and mana to keep going without rest.
text.veteran: Drain-tanking and Life Tap: almost no downtime.

text.newcomer: Curses, fear and drains wear enemies down.
text.veteran: DoT pressure plus Fear and Death Coil.

text.newcomer: Patient pressure: enemies wither while you stay safe.
Few big hits: your damage builds up over time.
Physically weak, so you rely on your demon to protect you.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Drains and a demon tank make leveling safe, if slow and steady.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Safe HC leveler with a Voidwalker.

newInForever: Improved Drains, Pandemic and Soul Siphon.
Curses of Agony and Doom become Banes.
scoreBasis: Classic-era leveling reputation (assumption) plus Forever's drain talents and Spirit-scaled Life Tap.

name: Demonology Warlock

pitch.newcomer: A demon master whose summoned minions fight and tank for them.
pitch.veteran: Pet-empowerment caster: Demonic Sacrifice and Pact, Demonic Brand tanking, Soul Fire.

text.newcomer: Your demons are powerful partners that grow with you.
text.veteran: Pets scale with your stats; Demonic Knowledge.

text.newcomer: Your Voidwalker can hold enemies while you cast.
text.veteran: Demonic Brand gives the Voidwalker high threat.

text.newcomer: Little downtime thanks to Life Tap and a healing demon.
text.veteran: Life Tap plus Demonic Energies sustain.

text.newcomer: Raid value depends on how demons perform at the endgame.
Managing demons adds more to think about.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: A demon tank between you and danger makes leveling safer.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Voidwalker tanking: safe HC leveling.

newInForever: Demonic Brand: pet attacks generate high threat.
scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption) plus Blizzard's note that Demonic Brand suits tanking pets like the Voidwalker.

name: Destruction Warlock

pitch.newcomer: A chaos caster who hurls fire and shadow for explosive damage.
pitch.veteran: Burst caster: Conflagrate, Shadowburn, Bane of Havoc, Incinerate.

text.newcomer: Explosive fire and shadow hits.
Strong damage for raids, splashing extra harm with Bane of Havoc.
A simple, punchy way to play a warlock.
Physically weak: if enemies reach you, you're in trouble.
More downtime than other warlocks.
Has a demon by default; sacrificing it for power is up to you.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Keep a demon out while leveling; going petless is risky.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Pet out on HC; Demonic Sacrifice later.

newInForever: Shadow and Flame links Conflagrate and Shadowburn.
Firestone and Spellstone are now weapon imbues.

variants.name: Demonic Sacrifice
variants.note: Sacrifice your demon for a 2-hour buff (Demonology 11-point) to play without a pet.

scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption) plus Incinerate and Bane of Havoc. Petless play via Demonic Sacrifice is assumed viable.

name: Balance Druid

pitch.newcomer: A moonkin star-caller who calls down moonfire and the wrath of nature.
pitch.veteran: Moonkin caster: Eclipse, Insect Swarm, raid-wide Moonkin aura.

text.newcomer: Buffs, battle resurrection and a raid-wide aura.
Can shift into a bear or travel form to escape trouble.
Eclipse rewards weaving Wrath and Starfire.
Uses a lot of mana, so expect breaks.
No slows or interrupts to stop enemies.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Forms and heals give you lots of ways to survive.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Forms + heals: flexible HC survival.

newInForever: Wrath is much cheaper to cast.
scoreBasis: Balance changed a lot in Forever (Eclipse, cheaper Wrath, raid-wide aura); Classic-era baseline (assumption) for the rest.

name: Feral Druid (Cat)

pitch.newcomer: A stalking cat who shreds prey from the shadows: sly, fast and fierce.
pitch.veteran: Energy and combo melee: Shifting Power powershifting, Berserk, bleeds.

text.newcomer: Shapeshifting heals and fast kills keep you moving.
Sneak past enemies to gather herbs and treasure.
text.veteran: Stealth plus travel form: an excellent farmer and gatherer.

text.newcomer: Rewards skill: master energy and form-shifting.
text.veteran: Shifting Power powershifting: high skill ceiling.

text.newcomer: Lots of timing to learn before it clicks.
Raid demand is uncertain.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Stealth, Dash and healing forms help you survive.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Prowl + Dash + heals: flexible HC escapes.

newInForever: Shifting Power (16-point) brings back a simpler powershifting.
Leader of the Pack is raid-wide.
Potions and weapon enchants work in forms.
scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption) plus Shifting Power and form quality-of-life changes; Shifting Power arrived late in the beta.

name: Feral Druid (Bear)

pitch.newcomer: A great bear who shields the group with thick hide and mighty roars.
pitch.veteran: Bear tank: Primal Bite, Lacerate, Frenzied Regeneration, reworked Thick Hide.

text.newcomer: Frenzied Regeneration heals you to full in a pinch.
text.veteran: Frenzied Regeneration: up to 100% health with rage.

text.newcomer: Tanks are always needed, and you can swap to cat or healer too.
Tough enough to carry the flag in battlegrounds.
Hard to kill, but not much of a threat to other players.
Raid tanking is still unproven.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Very tough to kill: one of the safest ways to tank on Hardcore.
hardcoreNote.veteran: High durability; strong HC tank.

newInForever: Natural Reaction: dodges can give rage.
scoreBasis: Classic-era baseline (assumption) plus Forever's bear tanking upgrades (Primal Bite, Frenzied Regeneration, Thick Hide).

name: Restoration Druid

pitch.newcomer: A nature healer who blankets allies in blooming heals over time.
pitch.veteran: HoT healer: Wild Growth, Swiftmend, Revive at 12.

text.newcomer: A healer every group wants.
text.veteran: Healer demand; Wild Growth group HoT.

text.newcomer: Hard to pin down in team PvP thanks to forms.
Healing over time that keeps everyone topped up.
Heals over time need planning ahead.
Slow alone; most level as Feral and swap later.

hardcoreNote.newcomer: Level as Feral and use dual spec at 40 for healing: flexible and safe.
hardcoreNote.veteran: Feral/Resto dual spec is the HC play.

newInForever: Swiftmend (16-point) no longer eats your HoT.
Gift of the Earthmother speeds up HoT casting.
scoreBasis: Classic-era healer baseline (assumption) plus Wild Growth, Swiftmend and Revive.
